Subject: HelixBi testimonial draft + quick fact-check

Hi Samantha —

Attached is the first public draft of the HelixBi customer story we discussed at the QBR. Thanks again for agreeing to participate — this will run as a customer spotlight on our site and in a short PDF we share with prospects.

Could you please do a quick pass for the following by end of week?
- Fact-check the three metrics called out in the executive summary (throughput, latency, and cost delta). I pulled from the post-migration summary but want your stamp.
- Approve or edit the short quote attributed to Tom (suggested below).
- Confirm any wording you’d prefer we don’t use (e.g., competitor names or specific customer KPIs you want kept internal).

Key snippets to verify: 
- "Throughput increased ~3–4x for batched inference workloads."
- "Tail p95 latency dropped to under 150ms for most models."
- "Unit inference cost decreased ~40% after moving to Redwood with caching and quantization."

Suggested Tom quote (please edit):
"Redwood helped us reduce inference cost while improving throughput and maintaining latency for critical models."

Attachments: Helix_Bi_case_draft_v2.docx (draft with highlights).

If you prefer, we can do a 20-min call tomorrow to walk through redlines. We’d also like permission to publish once you sign the short publication release (DocuSign link will follow).

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

From: Samantha Ruiz <samantha@helixbi.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@helixbi.com>
Date: 2026-04-17 11:04 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixBi testimonial draft + quick fact-check

Laura — thanks for the draft. We did a quick internal review and have a few redlines / factual corrections. Inline notes below.

On Tue, Apr 15, 2026 at 9:18 AM Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> Attached is the first public draft of the HelixBi customer story we discussed at the QBR.
> Could you please do a quick pass for the following by end of week?

Inline corrections:
- Throughput: accurate summary is closer to "~3x" on typical production workloads; peak batch throughput saw a 4x improvement but that was during a controlled test. Please change to "~3x on production traffic".
- Latency: our p95 measurements were ~120ms after the final tuning (not "under 150ms" is fine but please put the specific 120ms figure).
- Cost delta: the 40% number is optimistic; our finance team reports a 35% reduction in unit inference costs after caching + quantization. Please change to 35%.
- Please remove the sentence that references a competitor by name in paragraph 3 — we prefer a neutral comparison.

Suggested quote from Tom (for approval):
"Working with Redwood reduced our inference unit costs by 35% while enabling a threefold increase in steady-state throughput — all without compromising latency."

I attached the redlined version for reference: Helix_Bi_case_draft_v2_redlines.docx.

One more ask: our legal team needs to sign the standard publication release before you publish. Can you send the DocuSign?

Samantha Ruiz
Head of Product Communications, HelixBi
samantha@helixbi.com

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ruiz <samantha@helixbi.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-19 08:27 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixBi testimonial draft + quick fact-check

Thanks, Samantha — really helpful. I synced with engineering and finance to confirm: we are comfortable adopting HelixBi's corrected figures in the public draft (35% cost reduction; 120ms p95; "~3x" production throughput).

A few small editorial asks from our side that keep the technical accuracy but make the copy tighter:
- For clarity, replace "reduced our inference unit costs by 35%" with "reduced unit inference cost by 35% through prefix caching and INT8 quantization" — if you're okay with the added detail.
- Replace the phrase "deployed in under X weeks" (we had placeholder X) with the actual deployment window "8 weeks".

Proposed final customer quote (please confirm exact wording below so we can include it verbatim in the release and DocuSign):
"Redwood helped us reduce unit inference cost by 35% through caching and quantization, while delivering threefold steady-state throughput and 120ms p95 latency in production."

I've attached a preview image of the final quote layout (redwood-final-quote.png) and added the DocuSign link to the publication release: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/placeholder/abc123

If you confirm the quote text I will route the release to your legal for signature and then schedule publication.

Thanks again — small ask to sign and we’ll publish the HelixBi spotlight next week.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
